We have used weighted inverse_error, weighted softmax_neg_error, weighted w2 etc. We haven't tested weighted w1, w5, or median pool4, trimmed_mean pool4, dba pool4, weighted pool4 inverse_error, weighted pool4 softmax_neg_error. Let's pick something different: maybe weighted pool4 inverse_error. That uses a smaller pool of correlated groups. Let's test that.

attempts.rationale: Test a weighted combination with inverse_error to see if error-based weighting improves over simple mean, given unstable ranking.
test a robust median combination to handle unstable ranking and correlated errors.
Test a robust trimmed_mean combination to see if removing outlier models improves performance given unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
try a weighted combo with softmax_neg_error to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over trimmed mean; this is a different combination type.
ranking is unstable and several correlated groups exist, so a robust dba combination may improve over trimmed mean.
test a per‑horizon weighted scheme using the top‑k‑mean‑per‑horizon handle w4, which may capture changing best models across horizons.
Test a simple mean over the reduced, stable pool4 to see if removing weak, correlated models improves robustness in this unstable ranking scenario.
test a per‑horizon weighted combination using the top‑k‑per‑horizon handle (w7) to capture horizon‑specific strengths.
Test a weighted combination using the forward‑selection weight handle (w6) on the full pool to see if greedy forward weights outperform others given unstable ranking.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a per‑horizon weighted combination on the top‑stable pool4 may capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series has strong trend and seasonality but unstable ranking; a simple mean over all models may provide robustness.
The series shows unstable ranking and strong correlation groups; using a smaller pool of diverse models (pool4) with inverse-error weighting may improve robustness.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9994. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.17); 1 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.743.
